title: Charter of the United Nations
summary: Signed at San Francisco on 26 June 1945 by fifty states, the Charter is the founding treaty of the United Nations: a General Assembly of all members, a Security Council of five permanent members with a veto and a standing responsibility for peace and security, a Court, and a Trusteeship Council for the territories taken from the defeated empires. It bound members to settle disputes peacefully and to respect human rights and self-determination, and it made membership itself a thing the great powers could withhold. Portugal, neutral and authoritarian, was kept out for a decade; when it was finally admitted the Assembly's anti-colonial majority became the standing external pressure on its African policy.
